title: trk: give a store-load failure its own exit code, distinct from NoSuchId/BadId/AmbiguousId
body:
Discovered fixing Enix 01M40QAJ3 (closed-tracker-id-check still fails open).

src/main.zig:62-65 returns 1 when store.load() fails ("trk: failed to load store: ..."), and
main.zig:125-145 ALSO returns 1 for every ordinary CLI error (NoSuchId, BadId, AmbiguousId, ...).
Only CompactedId gets its own exit (2, main.zig:121). So any caller that branches on `trk show
<id>`'s exit code cannot tell "the id does not exist" from "the tracker store itself failed to
load" -- a corrupt/unreadable store looks identical, on exit code alone, to a clean not-found.

Enix's scripts/closed-tracker-id-check.sh (resolve_state, probe_trk) works around this with an
INTERIM fix: at rc 1, grep stderr for trk's own literal wording ("trk: failed to load store:") to
distinguish the two cases. That is fragile -- it depends on exact stderr text nothing commits trk
to keeping stable -- and the structural fix is a distinct exit code (e.g. 3) for store.load()
failure, separate from the CliError-returns-1 bucket and from CompactedId's 2.

Scope: give main.zig's store.load() failure path its own exit code; update the CLI's documented
exit-code contract (main.zig's own header comment, and any --help text that states it). Once
that exists, Enix's closed-tracker-id-check.sh stderr-text match can be simplified or dropped.

title: rule: a structured 'by' field on the ruling event (scott | rec-bot + cited ids), so provenance is a field check, not prose
body:
Raised by the Enix tracker's decision 01M35NGPJ. Scott ruled on 2026-10-15 how rec-bot should work; the full ruling and his words are on Enix task 01M50DBW6.
A ruling records WHAT was decided, and WHO ruled is a structured field on the rule event:
- by: scott -- the orchestrator recording his answer. 'go with rec' is stored as the adopted ruling text.
- by: rec-bot -- together with cites: [<ruled decision ids / doc#section>], a closure by citation.
Then 'can this decision be traced to Scott' is a walk: follow cites until every leaf is a by-scott ruling or a doc ruling.
Scope: the rule CLI flag and the MCP parameter, show/list/--json exposure, and a query for rulings with no path back to Scott. Enix's rec-bot skill and lint then read this field instead of the interim prose prefix 'RULED BY REC-BOT, cites: ...'.
